Text:
Kisah Warga Kemalingan Motor : Seminggu Setelah Laporan, Polisi Tak Datang ke TKP, Baru Muncul Setelah Beritanya Viral di TV

----------------------------------------------------------------------

Kisah ini terjadi di Kebayoran Baru, Jakarta Selatan.

Seorang warga, yang kebetulan anggota TNI, yakni Sertu Mualimin kehilangan sepeda motor di rumahnya, Jalan Dasa IV, Kebayoran Baru, Jaksel pada 17 Agustus 2025.

Karena kesal polisi tak bergerak, ia membuat sayembara sendiri.

Siapa yang menemukan motor iu, dapat hadiah.

Tatu, sang istri, mengatakan pihak kepolisian tak cepat bergerak meski sudah ada laporan.

Tatu menyoroti polisi yang tak kunjung melakukan olah TKP di rumahnya untuk mengambil sidik jari pelaku di pagar rumahnya. 

Padahal, orang rumah sudah bela-belain untuk mensterilkan TKP.

“Sidik jari pasti kan masih ada orang-orang, belum ada yang megang pas hari itu. Tapi belum ada (polisi) sampai sekarang ke sini,” kata dia, dikutip dari Kompas-com, Selasa (26/8/2025). 

Empat hari usai kejadian, Tatu sempat kedatangan dua wartawan media televisi swasta. 

Tatu mengira itu adalah penyidik dari Polres Jakarta Selatan. 

Setelah kejadian itu ditayangkan di televisi, eh, tim kepolisian baru menghubungi Mualimin untuk datang ke Mapolres Jakarta Selatan. 

“Udah viral di TV, baru dia gerak. kemarin suami saya dapat kabar dari Polres, ada panggilan. Kemarin ke mana saja? Masa sudah seminggu belum olah TKP,” keluh Tatu. 

Terpisah, Kasi Humas Polres Jakarta Selatan, Kompol Murodih, menyebutkan bahwa kasus pencurian motor tersebut sedang dalam penyelidikan oleh Unit Reserse Kriminal. 

“Untuk ini (laporan curanmor) masih kami lidik,” kata Murodih saat dikonfirmasi, Senin.

Baiknya anggaran Polri rp 100 triliun dihapus.
Polisi sdh tidak melayani, melindungi, dan mengayomi masyarakat.
Malu makan gaji buta
author: Agus Nizami

Travel memory: Good morning, virtual adventurers! Today is Friday, May 8, 2026, and I’m really looking forward to taking you on a spectacular journey into the heart of Portuguese history. Our virtual adventure takes us to one of Lisbon’s most famous landmarks—the Tower of Belém, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its majestic beauty, fascinating legends, and historical significance. Get ready for an immersive exploration of this architectural masterpiece, which once served as Portugal’s gateway to the world. Let’s dive in and uncover the secrets behind this mythical tower, which has stood steadfast on the banks of the Tagus for centuries!

A Symbol of Power and the Spirit of Discovery - Built between 1514 and 1519 under King Manuel I, the Tower of Belém was originally intended as a coastal fortification to protect Lisbon from naval attacks. However, it became far more than just a military structure. Richly decorated with motifs in the Manueline style—including twisted ropes, Crosses of the Order of Christ, and armillary spheres—the tower embodied Portugal’s maritime supremacy during the Age of Discovery. Strategically located at the river’s mouth, the Torre de Belém witnessed fleets full of explorers, spices, and treasures setting sail for distant lands—and welcomed them back as symbols of Portugal’s global reach. When you imagine its observation decks, reminiscent of ship decks, and the ornate decorations inspired by exotic cultures, it quickly becomes clear how the tower visually reflects the spirit of adventure that defined this era.

The Rhinoceros Sculpture: A Story of Cultural Fusion - Among the many stories engraved in the stone of this monument, one particularly fascinating detail awaits discovery—a rhinoceros carved into the north facade. This sculpture depicts a real rhinoceros that was gifted to King Manuel I by an Indian ruler in 1515. Although the rhinoceros was tragically lost at sea on its way to Rome, it left an indelible legacy. It inspired Albrecht Dürer’s famous drawings and found eternal life in the carvings of the Torre de Belém. This seemingly small detail reveals a broader truth about Portugal’s maritime adventures: these voyages were not merely about claiming land; they also brought with them animals, ideas, and cultural exchange that forever altered the fabric of Europe.

Myths Surrounding the Tagus and the Tower - A captivating legend surrounding the Torre de Belém claims that it was originally built in the middle of the Tagus but was moved closer to the shore after the devastating earthquake of 1755. In reality, the truth lies in the subtle shifts of the coastline over the centuries. The tower was built on a small island near the coast, which gradually expanded and connected the structure to the mainland. Even though debunking this myth does not diminish its charm, the image of a tower rising from the water contributes to its mystical appeal—a lasting symbol of how Portugal once ruled the vast oceans.

The Tower’s Dark Chapters - Aside from its romantic and adventurous past, the tower also harbors darker stories. In its later years, the Torre de Belém served as a prison, particularly under the reign of King Miguel I in the 19th century. Its cold chambers—originally intended for storing weapons—were repurposed to imprison political opponents and dissidents. These haunting episodes remind us that even places of grandeur have their dark sides. The contrasting layers of light and darkness in the tower’s history make it all the more fascinating—a reflection of Portugal’s struggles and triumphs over time.

An Architectural Journey Through Time - The Torre de Belém embodies centuries of architectural evolution. Under the architect Francisco de Arruda, influences from Moorish art were integrated, evident in the geometric patterns, ribbed domes, and elegant arcades that adorn its structure. Later, in the 19th century, romantic embellishments accentuated its Manueline style, transforming the fortress into a feast for the eyes. As you admire the intricate details, you’ll notice how the tower serves as a bridge between eras, combining defensive purpose with breathtaking craftsmanship—a true architectural time capsule.

One of the Seven Wonders of Portugal - It comes as no surprise that the Torre de Belém was named “One of the Seven Wonders of Portugal” in 2007. Tourists flock here not only for its historical significance but also for the breathtaking panoramic view it offers over the Tagus River. Thousands climb to its summit every year to marvel at a landmark that stands as both a physical and symbolic gateway to Portugal’s glorious past.

A Living Time Capsule - The Torre de Belém defies the passage of time; its walls preserve the essence of Portuguese identity. From its role in the Age of Discovery, through its time as a prison, to its designation as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, the tower embodies courage, innovation, and the spirit of discovery. When you step inside, it feels as though you’re entering another world—a world where the echoes of distant voyages mingle with the whispers of those who once walked its corridors.

Your Gateway to History - The Torre de Belém is not just a building—it is a testament to Portugal’s boldness, creativity, and resilience. Whether you are drawn to its historical significance, its architectural beauty, or the legends that surround it, you are guaranteed to leave feeling inspired. 

Thank you so much for joining me on today’s virtual adventure! Tomorrow we’ll embark on a new journey to discover another treasure of our shared human history. Until then, I wish you a wonderful day. Best regards, Freddy Kalder

Souvenir de voyage : Bonjour, aventuriers virtuels ! Nous sommes aujourd’hui vendredi 8 mai 2026, et j’ai vraiment hâte de vous emmener dans un voyage spectaculaire au cœur de l’histoire du Portugal. Notre aventure virtuelle nous conduit vers l’un des monuments les plus célèbres de Lisbonne : la Tour de Belém, classée au patrimoine mondial de l’UNESCO, réputée pour sa beauté majestueuse, ses légendes fascinantes et son importance historique. Préparez-vous à une exploration immersive de ce chef-d’œuvre architectural, qui servait autrefois de porte d’entrée du Portugal sur le monde. Plongeons-nous dans cette tour mythique et découvrons ses secrets, qui se dresse fièrement sur les rives du Tage depuis des siècles !

Un symbole de puissance et de l'esprit de découverte - Construite entre 1514 et 1519 sous le règne du roi Manuel Ier, la tour de Belém était à l'origine destinée à servir de fortification côtière pour protéger Lisbonne des attaques navales. Cependant, elle est devenue bien plus qu'une simple structure militaire. Richement décorée de motifs de style manuélin — notamment des cordes torsadées, des croix de l’Ordre du Christ et des sphères armillaires —, la tour incarnait la suprématie maritime du Portugal à l’époque des grandes découvertes. Stratégiquement située à l’embouchure du fleuve, la Torre de Belém a vu des flottes chargées d’explorateurs, d’épices et de trésors mettre le cap vers des contrées lointaines — et les a accueillies à leur retour comme symboles de l’influence mondiale du Portugal. Lorsque l’on imagine ses ponts d’observation, qui rappellent ceux des navires, et ses décorations somptueuses inspirées de cultures exotiques, on comprend rapidement à quel point la tour reflète visuellement l’esprit d’aventure qui a défini cette époque.

La sculpture du rhinocéros : une histoire de fusion culturelle - Parmi les nombreuses histoires gravées dans la pierre de ce monument, un détail particulièrement fascinant attend d’être découvert : un rhinocéros sculpté sur la façade nord. Cette sculpture représente un véritable rhinocéros offert au roi Manuel Ier par un souverain indien en 1515. Bien que le rhinocéros ait tragiquement péri en mer alors qu’il était en route pour Rome, il a laissé un héritage indélébile. Il a inspiré les célèbres dessins d’Albrecht Dürer et a trouvé une vie éternelle dans les sculptures de la Torre de Belém. Ce détail en apparence insignifiant révèle une vérité plus large sur les aventures maritimes du Portugal : ces voyages ne visaient pas seulement à revendiquer des terres ; ils ont également apporté avec eux des animaux, des idées et des échanges culturels qui ont bouleversé à jamais le tissu de l’Europe.

Mythes entourant le Tage et la tour - Une légende captivante entourant la Torre de Belém prétend qu’elle fut à l’origine construite au milieu du Tage, mais qu’elle fut déplacée plus près du rivage après le tremblement de terre dévastateur de 1755. En réalité, la vérité réside dans les subtils changements du littoral au fil des siècles. La tour a été construite sur une petite île près de la côte, qui s’est progressivement étendue et a relié la structure au continent. Même si le fait de démystifier ce mythe n’enlève rien à son charme, l’image d’une tour s’élevant de l’eau contribue à son attrait mystique — un symbole durable de la façon dont le Portugal régnait autrefois sur les vastes océans.

Les chapitres sombres de la tour - Outre son passé romantique et aventureux, la tour recèle également des histoires plus sombres. Au cours de ses dernières années, la Torre de Belém a servi de prison, en particulier sous le règne du roi Miguel Ier au XIXe siècle. Ses chambres froides — initialement destinées au stockage des armes — ont été réaffectées pour emprisonner les opposants politiques et les dissidents. Ces épisodes obsédants nous rappellent que même les lieux de grandeur ont leurs côtés sombres. Les contrastes entre lumière et obscurité qui marquent l’histoire de la tour la rendent d’autant plus fascinante : elle est le reflet des luttes et des triomphes du Portugal au fil du temps.

Un voyage architectural à travers le temps - La Torre de Belém incarne des siècles d’évolution architecturale. Sous la direction de l’architecte Francisco de Arruda, des influences de l’art mauresque ont été intégrées, comme en témoignent les motifs géométriques, les dômes nervurés et les élégantes arcades qui ornent sa structure. Plus tard, au XIXe siècle, des ornements romantiques ont accentué son style manuélin, transformant la forteresse en un véritable régal pour les yeux. En admirant les détails complexes, vous remarquerez comment la tour sert de pont entre les époques, alliant fonction défensive et savoir-faire artisanal époustouflant : une véritable capsule temporelle architecturale.

L'une des sept merveilles du Portugal - Il n'est pas surprenant que la Torre de Belém ait été désignée « l'une des sept merveilles du Portugal » en 2007. Les touristes s'y pressent non seulement pour son importance historique, mais aussi pour la vue panoramique à couper le souffle qu'elle offre sur le Tage. Des milliers de personnes gravissent son sommet chaque année pour s'émerveiller devant un monument qui se dresse comme une porte d'entrée à la fois physique et symbolique vers le glorieux passé du Portugal.

Une capsule temporelle vivante – La Torre de Belém défie le temps ; ses murs préservent l’essence de l’identité portugaise. De son rôle à l’époque des grandes découvertes, en passant par son utilisation comme prison, jusqu’à son inscription au patrimoine mondial de l’UNESCO, la tour incarne le courage, l’innovation et l’esprit de découverte. Lorsque vous y pénétrez, vous avez l’impression d’entrer dans un autre monde — un monde où les échos de voyages lointains se mêlent aux murmures de ceux qui ont autrefois arpenté ses couloirs.

Votre porte d’entrée vers l’histoire - La Torre de Belém n’est pas seulement un bâtiment — c’est un témoignage de l’audace, de la créativité et de la résilience du Portugal. Que vous soyez attiré par son importance historique, sa beauté architecturale ou les légendes qui l'entourent, vous repartirez à coup sûr inspiré.

Merci beaucoup de m'avoir accompagné dans cette aventure virtuelle d'aujourd'hui ! Demain, nous embarquerons pour un nouveau voyage à la découverte d'un autre trésor de notre histoire humaine commune. D'ici là, je vous souhaite une merveilleuse journée. Cordialement, Freddy Kalder

Ricordo di viaggio: Buongiorno, avventurieri virtuali! Oggi è venerdì 8 maggio 2026 e non vedo l’ora di accompagnarvi in un viaggio spettacolare nel cuore della storia portoghese. La nostra avventura virtuale ci porta in uno dei monumenti più famosi di Lisbona: la Torre di Belém, patrimonio mondiale dell’UNESCO, nota per la sua maestosa bellezza, le affascinanti leggende e il suo significato storico. Preparatevi a un'esplorazione immersiva di questo capolavoro architettonico, che un tempo fungeva da porta d'accesso del Portogallo al mondo. Immergiamoci e scopriamo i segreti che si celano dietro questa torre mitica, che da secoli si erge impassibile sulle rive del Tago!

Un simbolo di potere e dello spirito di scoperta - Costruita tra il 1514 e il 1519 sotto il re Manuele I, la Torre di Belém era originariamente concepita come fortificazione costiera per proteggere Lisbona dagli attacchi navali. Tuttavia, divenne molto più di una semplice struttura militare. Riccamente decorata con motivi in stile manuelino — tra cui corde intrecciate, croci dell’Ordine di Cristo e sfere armillari — la torre incarnava la supremazia marittima del Portogallo durante l’Era delle Scoperte. Situata strategicamente alla foce del fiume, la Torre di Belém ha visto flotte piene di esploratori, spezie e tesori salpare verso terre lontane — e le ha accolte al ritorno come simboli della portata globale del Portogallo. Se si immaginano i suoi ponti di osservazione, che ricordano i ponti delle navi, e le decorazioni ornate ispirate a culture esotiche, diventa subito chiaro come la torre rifletta visivamente lo spirito di avventura che ha caratterizzato quell’epoca.

La scultura del rinoceronte: una storia di fusione culturale - Tra le tante storie incise nella pietra di questo monumento, un dettaglio particolarmente affascinante attende di essere scoperto: un rinoceronte scolpito sulla facciata nord. Questa scultura raffigura un rinoceronte reale che fu donato al re Manuele I da un sovrano indiano nel 1515. Sebbene il rinoceronte andò tragicamente perduto in mare durante il viaggio verso Roma, lasciò un'eredità indelebile. Ispirò i famosi disegni di Albrecht Dürer e trovò vita eterna nelle sculture della Torre di Belém. Questo dettaglio apparentemente piccolo rivela una verità più ampia sulle avventure marittime del Portogallo: questi viaggi non miravano solo a rivendicare territori, ma portarono con sé anche animali, idee e scambi culturali che hanno cambiato per sempre il tessuto dell’Europa.

Miti sul Tago e sulla Torre - Un’affascinante leggenda sulla Torre di Belém sostiene che fosse stata originariamente costruita in mezzo al Tago, ma che sia stata spostata più vicino alla riva dopo il devastante terremoto del 1755. In realtà, la verità risiede nei sottili cambiamenti della linea costiera nel corso dei secoli. La torre fu costruita su una piccola isola vicino alla costa, che si espanse gradualmente e collegò la struttura alla terraferma. Anche se sfatare questo mito non ne diminuisce il fascino, l’immagine di una torre che sorge dall’acqua contribuisce al suo fascino mistico: un simbolo duraturo di come il Portogallo un tempo dominasse i vasti oceani.

I capitoli oscuri della Torre - Oltre al suo passato romantico e avventuroso, la torre custodisce anche storie più cupe. Negli ultimi anni, la Torre di Belém fu utilizzata come prigione, in particolare sotto il regno di re Miguel I nel XIX secolo. Le sue fredde celle, originariamente destinate al deposito delle armi, furono riadattate per imprigionare oppositori politici e dissidenti. Questi episodi inquietanti ci ricordano che anche i luoghi maestosi hanno i loro lati oscuri. I contrasti tra luce e oscurità nella storia della torre la rendono ancora più affascinante: un riflesso delle lotte e dei trionfi del Portogallo nel corso del tempo.

Un viaggio architettonico nel tempo - La Torre di Belém incarna secoli di evoluzione architettonica. Sotto la guida dell'architetto Francisco de Arruda, furono integrate influenze dell'arte moresca, evidenti nei motivi geometrici, nelle cupole a costoloni e negli eleganti portici che adornano la sua struttura. Più tardi, nel XIX secolo, abbellimenti romantici ne accentuarono lo stile manuelino, trasformando la fortezza in una festa per gli occhi. Ammirando i dettagli intricati, noterete come la torre funga da ponte tra le epoche, combinando lo scopo difensivo con un'artigianalità mozzafiato: una vera e propria capsula del tempo architettonica.

Una delle sette meraviglie del Portogallo - Non sorprende che la Torre di Belém sia stata nominata “Una delle sette meraviglie del Portogallo” nel 2007. I turisti accorrono qui non solo per il suo significato storico, ma anche per la vista panoramica mozzafiato che offre sul fiume Tago. Migliaia di persone salgono sulla sua cima ogni anno per ammirare un punto di riferimento che rappresenta una porta d’accesso sia fisica che simbolica al glorioso passato del Portogallo.

Una capsula del tempo vivente - La Torre di Belém sfida il passare del tempo; le sue mura conservano l’essenza dell’identità portoghese. Dal suo ruolo nell’Era delle Scoperte, passando per il periodo in cui fu utilizzata come prigione, fino alla sua designazione come Patrimonio Mondiale dell’UNESCO, la torre incarna il coraggio, l’innovazione e lo spirito di scoperta. Quando si entra, sembra di entrare in un altro mondo: un mondo in cui gli echi di viaggi lontani si mescolano ai sussurri di coloro che un tempo percorrevano i suoi corridoi.

La vostra porta d’accesso alla storia - La Torre di Belém non è solo un edificio: è una testimonianza dell’audacia, della creatività e della resilienza del Portogallo. Che siate attratti dal suo significato storico, dalla sua bellezza architettonica o dalle leggende che la circondano, ne uscirete sicuramente ispirati.

Grazie mille per avermi accompagnato nell'avventura virtuale di oggi! Domani intraprenderemo un nuovo viaggio alla scoperta di un altro tesoro della nostra storia umana comune. Nel frattempo, vi auguro una splendida giornata. Cordiali saluti, Freddy Kalder

Recuerdo de viaje: ¡Buenos días, aventureros virtuales! Hoy es viernes, 8 de mayo de 2026, y tengo muchas ganas de llevaros a un viaje espectacular al corazón de la historia portuguesa. Nuestra aventura virtual nos lleva a uno de los monumentos más famosos de Lisboa: la Torre de Belém, declarada Patrimonio de la Humanidad por la UNESCO y conocida por su majestuosa belleza, sus fascinantes leyendas y su importancia histórica. Prepárense para una exploración inmersiva de esta obra maestra arquitectónica, que en su día sirvió como puerta de entrada de Portugal al mundo. ¡Sumérjanse y descubran los secretos que se esconden tras esta mítica torre, que se ha mantenido firme a orillas del Tajo durante siglos!

Un símbolo de poder y del espíritu de descubrimiento - Construida entre 1514 y 1519 bajo el reinado del rey Manuel I, la Torre de Belém se concibió originalmente como una fortificación costera para proteger Lisboa de los ataques navales. Sin embargo, se convirtió en mucho más que una simple estructura militar. Ricamente decorada con motivos de estilo manuelino —como cuerdas retorcidas, cruces de la Orden de Cristo y esferas armilares—, la torre encarnaba la supremacía marítima de Portugal durante la Era de los Descubrimientos. Estratégicamente situada en la desembocadura del río, la Torre de Belém fue testigo de cómo flotas repletas de exploradores, especias y tesoros zarpaban hacia tierras lejanas, y les daba la bienvenida a su regreso como símbolo del alcance global de Portugal. Cuando uno imagina sus miradores, que recuerdan a las cubiertas de los barcos, y las ornamentadas decoraciones inspiradas en culturas exóticas, rápidamente queda claro cómo la torre refleja visualmente el espíritu de aventura que definió esta época.

La escultura del rinoceronte: una historia de fusión cultural - Entre las muchas historias grabadas en la piedra de este monumento, hay un detalle particularmente fascinante por descubrir: un rinoceronte tallado en la fachada norte. Esta escultura representa un rinoceronte real que fue regalado al rey Manuel I por un gobernante indio en 1515. Aunque el rinoceronte se perdió trágicamente en el mar de camino a Roma, dejó un legado indeleble. Inspiró los famosos dibujos de Alberto Durero y encontró la vida eterna en las tallas de la Torre de Belém. Este detalle aparentemente insignificante revela una verdad más amplia sobre las aventuras marítimas de Portugal: estos viajes no se limitaban a la conquista de territorios, sino que también trajeron consigo animales, ideas e intercambios culturales que alteraron para siempre el tejido de Europa.

Mitos en torno al Tajo y la Torre - Una cautivadora leyenda sobre la Torre de Belém afirma que fue construida originalmente en medio del Tajo, pero que se trasladó más cerca de la orilla tras el devastador terremoto de 1755. En realidad, la verdad reside en los sutiles cambios de la línea costera a lo largo de los siglos. La torre se construyó en una pequeña isla cerca de la costa, que se fue ampliando gradualmente y conectó la estructura con el continente. Aunque desmontar este mito no le resta encanto, la imagen de una torre que se eleva sobre el agua contribuye a su atractivo místico: un símbolo perdurable de cómo Portugal gobernó en su día los vastos océanos.

Los capítulos oscuros de la torre - Aparte de su pasado romántico y aventurero, la torre también alberga historias más sombrías. En sus últimos años, la Torre de Belém sirvió como prisión, especialmente bajo el reinado del rey Miguel I en el siglo XIX. Sus frías cámaras —destinadas originalmente al almacenamiento de armas— se reconvirtieron para encarcelar a opositores políticos y disidentes. Estos episodios inquietantes nos recuerdan que incluso los lugares grandiosos tienen su lado oscuro. Las capas contrastantes de luz y oscuridad en la historia de la torre la hacen aún más fascinante: un reflejo de las luchas y los triunfos de Portugal a lo largo del tiempo.

Un viaje arquitectónico a través del tiempo - La Torre de Belém encarna siglos de evolución arquitectónica. Bajo la dirección del arquitecto Francisco de Arruda, se integraron influencias del arte morisco, evidentes en los patrones geométricos, las cúpulas acanaladas y las elegantes arcadas que adornan su estructura. Más tarde, en el siglo XIX, los adornos románticos acentuaron su estilo manuelino, transformando la fortaleza en un festín para la vista. Al admirar los intrincados detalles, se dará cuenta de cómo la torre sirve de puente entre épocas, combinando su función defensiva con una artesanía impresionante: una auténtica cápsula del tiempo arquitectónica.

Una de las Siete Maravillas de Portugal - No es de extrañar que la Torre de Belém fuera nombrada «Una de las Siete Maravillas de Portugal» en 2007. Los turistas acuden en masa no solo por su importancia histórica, sino también por la impresionante vista panorámica que ofrece sobre el río Tajo. Miles de personas suben a su cima cada año para maravillarse ante un hito que se erige como puerta de entrada, tanto física como simbólica, al glorioso pasado de Portugal.

Una cápsula del tiempo viviente: la Torre de Belém desafía el paso del tiempo; sus muros conservan la esencia de la identidad portuguesa. Desde su papel en la Era de los Descubrimientos, pasando por su etapa como prisión, hasta su designación como Patrimonio de la Humanidad por la UNESCO, la torre encarna el coraje, la innovación y el espíritu de descubrimiento. Al entrar, se tiene la sensación de estar entrando en otro mundo, un mundo donde los ecos de viajes lejanos se mezclan con los susurros de quienes una vez recorrieron sus pasillos.

Tu puerta de entrada a la historia: la Torre de Belém no es solo un edificio, es un testimonio de la audacia, la creatividad y la resiliencia de Portugal. Tanto si te atrae su importancia histórica, su belleza arquitectónica o las leyendas que la rodean, te garantizo que saldrás de allí sintiéndote inspirado.

¡Muchas gracias por acompañarme en la aventura virtual de hoy! Mañana nos embarcaremos en un nuevo viaje para descubrir otro tesoro de nuestra historia humana compartida. Hasta entonces, te deseo un día maravilloso. Un saludo, Freddy Kalder

A nossa aventura virtual leva-nos a um dos monumentos mais famosos de Lisboa — a Torre de Belém, Património Mundial da UNESCO, conhecida pela sua beleza majestosa, lendas fascinantes e importância histórica. Preparem-se para uma exploração imersiva desta obra-prima arquitetónica, que outrora serviu de porta de entrada de Portugal para o mundo. Vamos mergulhar e desvendar os segredos por trás desta torre mítica, que se ergue firme nas margens do Tejo há séculos!

Um símbolo de poder e do espírito de descoberta - Construída entre 1514 e 1519 sob o reinado de D. Manuel I, a Torre de Belém foi originalmente concebida como uma fortificação costeira para proteger Lisboa de ataques navais. No entanto, tornou-se muito mais do que uma simples estrutura militar. Ricamente decorada com motivos de estilo manuelino — incluindo cordas torcidas, cruzes da Ordem de Cristo e esferas armilares —, a torre encarnava a supremacia marítima de Portugal durante a Era dos Descobrimentos. Estrategicamente localizada na foz do rio, a Torre de Belém testemunhou frotas repletas de exploradores, especiarias e tesouros a zarpar para terras distantes — e deu-lhes as boas-vindas de regresso como símbolos do alcance global de Portugal. Quando imaginamos os seus miradouros, que lembram os conveses dos navios, e as decorações ornamentadas inspiradas em culturas exóticas, torna-se rapidamente claro como a torre reflete visualmente o espírito de aventura que definiu esta era.

A Escultura do Rinoceronte: Uma História de Fusão Cultural — Entre as muitas histórias gravadas na pedra deste monumento, um detalhe particularmente fascinante aguarda ser descoberto — um rinoceronte esculpido na fachada norte. Esta escultura retrata um rinoceronte real que foi oferecido ao rei D. Manuel I por um governante indiano em 1515. Embora o rinoceronte tenha tragicamente desaparecido no mar a caminho de Roma, deixou um legado indelével. Inspirou os famosos desenhos de Albrecht Dürer e encontrou vida eterna nas esculturas da Torre de Belém. Este detalhe aparentemente pequeno revela uma verdade mais ampla sobre as aventuras marítimas de Portugal: estas viagens não se resumiam apenas à conquista de terras; trouxeram também consigo animais, ideias e intercâmbio cultural que alteraram para sempre a estrutura da Europa.

Mitos em torno do Tejo e da Torre — Uma lenda cativante em torno da Torre de Belém afirma que esta foi originalmente construída no meio do Tejo, mas foi deslocada para mais perto da costa após o devastador terramoto de 1755. Na realidade, a verdade reside nas subtis alterações da linha costeira ao longo dos séculos. A torre foi construída numa pequena ilha perto da costa, que se expandiu gradualmente e ligou a estrutura ao continente. Embora desmascarar este mito não diminua o seu encanto, a imagem de uma torre a erguer-se da água contribui para o seu apelo místico — um símbolo duradouro de como Portugal outrora dominou os vastos oceanos.

Os Capítulos Negros da Torre — Para além do seu passado romântico e aventureiro, a torre também guarda histórias mais sombrias. Nos seus últimos anos, a Torre de Belém serviu de prisão, particularmente sob o reinado do rei D. Miguel I, no século XIX. As suas câmaras frias — originalmente destinadas ao armazenamento de armas — foram reaproveitadas para aprisionar opositores políticos e dissidentes. Estes episódios assombrosos lembram-nos que mesmo os locais de grandeza têm os seus lados sombrios. As camadas contrastantes de luz e escuridão na história da torre tornam-na ainda mais fascinante — um reflexo das lutas e triunfos de Portugal ao longo do tempo.

Uma viagem arquitetónica através do tempo — A Torre de Belém encarna séculos de evolução arquitetónica. Sob a orientação do arquiteto Francisco de Arruda, foram integradas influências da arte mourisca, evidentes nos padrões geométricos, nas cúpulas nervuradas e nas elegantes arcadas que adornam a sua estrutura. Mais tarde, no século XIX, os ornamentos românticos acentuaram o seu estilo manuelino, transformando a fortaleza num deleite para os olhos. Ao admirar os detalhes intricados, irá notar como a torre serve de ponte entre épocas, combinando a finalidade defensiva com um artesanato de tirar o fôlego — uma verdadeira cápsula do tempo arquitetónica.

Uma das Sete Maravilhas de Portugal — Não é surpresa que a Torre de Belém tenha sido nomeada «Uma das Sete Maravilhas de Portugal» em 2007. Os turistas acorrem aqui não só pelo seu significado histórico, mas também pela vista panorâmica de tirar o fôlego que oferece sobre o rio Tejo. Milhares de pessoas sobem ao seu cume todos os anos para se maravilharem com um marco que se ergue como uma porta de entrada, tanto física como simbólica, para o passado glorioso de Portugal.

Uma Cápsula do Tempo Viva — A Torre de Belém desafia a passagem do tempo; as suas paredes preservam a essência da identidade portuguesa. Desde o seu papel na Era dos Descobrimentos, passando pelo seu período como prisão, até à sua designação como Património Mundial da UNESCO, a torre personifica a coragem, a inovação e o espírito de descoberta. Ao entrar, sente-se como se estivesse a entrar noutro mundo — um mundo onde os ecos de viagens distantes se misturam com os sussurros daqueles que outrora percorreram os seus corredores.

A sua porta de entrada para a história — A Torre de Belém não é apenas um edifício — é um testemunho da ousadia, criatividade e resiliência de Portugal. Quer seja atraído pelo seu significado histórico, pela sua beleza arquitetónica ou pelas lendas que a rodeiam, garantidamente sairá de lá inspirado.

Muito obrigado por se juntar a mim nesta aventura virtual de hoje! Amanhã embarcaremos numa nova viagem para descobrir outro tesouro da nossa história humana comum. Até lá, desejo-lhe um dia maravilhoso. Cumprimentos, Freddy Kalder

Habib Ahmad Tulungagung Sudah Mengetahui Jam Wafatnya

Wali memang tidak takut mati. Bahkan ketika umurnya akan penuh (wafat), mereka sudah menyiapkan diri. Termasuk Habib Ahmad Salim Al-Muhdlor, Desa Domasan, Kaligawen, Tulungagung, Jawa Timur.

Kepada Kiai Khoirul (seorang ulama), Habib Ahmad pernah menyatakan bahwa ia, pada jam 12 siang saat bertemu Kiai Khoirul, akan meninggal. Terang saja Kiai Khoirul tidak percaya begitu saja.

"Mau meninggal kok tidak pakai pendahuluan Bib, sakit atau apa begitu," kata Kiai Khoirul.

Mereka berdua masih ngobrol, dan tanpa ada tanda wafat sama sakali, Habib Ahmad tetap saja asyik ngobrol bersama Kiai Koirul sampai 11.30, hanya kurang 30an menit seperti dikatakan.

"Ini kurang lima menit loh, Bib," tanya Kiai Khoirul.

"Iya, ini Izra'il sudah datang," jawab Habib Ahmad, "tapi sebelum meninggal, aku ingin buat perjanjian sama kamu," lanjut Habib Ahmad.

"Perjanjian apa Bib?" Kiai Khoirul makin dibuat heran, karena hanya kurang 5 menitan beliau akan meninggal.

Habib Ahmad membuat perjanjian ke Kiai Khoirul. Ini perjanjiannnya:

Bila kamu di akhirat besok lebih nikmat dari aku, maka aku ikut kamu, tapi bila aku lebih nikmat, kamu harus ikut aku. 

Sebelum seminggu kamu meninggal, aku akan akan datang memberitahumu.

Benar saja, setelah kesepakatan itu diucapakan, Habib Ahmad langsung meninggal. Tiba-tiba saja beliau terlihat seperti lemas, bersandar ke ke tembok dan wafat seketika. Innalillah wa inna ilahi raji'un.

Habib Ahmad Salim Al-Muhdlor Tulungagung wafat pas seperti dikatakan, jam 12 persis. Dan, sebelum Kiai Khoirul wafat pun, beliau memang ditemui Habib Ahmad (dalam kondisi setengah sadar dan tidak) kalau sepekan lagi ia harus siap dijemput Izra'il dengan jalan kepleset di rumah.

***

Cerita lain juga datang dari Mbah Dimyathi Comal, guru Habib Luthfi bin Yahya, yang pernah memberitahukan waktu wafatnya dengan bahasa pengantin.

"Bib, seminggu lagi akan jadi pengantin. Itu tempatnya," kata Mbah Dimyathi ke Habib Luthfi sambil menunjuk calon lokasi pemakaman.

Sumber: dutaislam. or .id

HK, de son vrai nom Kaddour Hadadi, parcourt les routes de France en musique depuis plusieurs décennies. Dans sa besace : de la révolte, une sincérité à toute épreuve, et beaucoup d’amour. Bilan de plus de trente ans de combat.

Révélé au grand public dans les années 1990 avec MAP (Ministère des Affaires Populaires), le chanteur HK continue sa carrière en solo, en duo ou entouré de dizaines de « Saltimbanks ». En 2021, nous l’avions rencontré lors d’un rassemblement en Ardèche, en pleine crise du Covid-19. Sa chanson Danser encore avait alors déjà cumulé plusieurs millions de vues sur YouTube.

Cinq ans plus tard, HK est toujours là pour dénoncer l’absurde, les inégalités, la xénophobie, les entraves à nos libertés fondamentales. Depuis, il a également constaté à quel point les médias hexagonaux avaient changé : auparavant célébrés, ses musiciens et lui ont été peu à peu boudés, mis de côté par de nombreuses chaînes de télévision et de radios « mainstream ». 

Dans son dernier album, Le Coeur au vent, HK mise sur la poésie des mots pour rappeler la nécessité de rester soudés, les dangers de la propagande ou le combat pour la démocratie. Il met également en musique le poème Il vous appartiendra de vivre, de l’écrivain Refaat Alareer, né et mort à Gaza, un pays qu’il n’a jamais voulu quitter.

Rencontre avec un artiste profondément intègre, qui ne lâchera jamais rien.

➡ Mr Mondialisation : Peux-tu nous raconter un peu ton parcours, l’environnement dans lequel tu as grandi et qui a forgé la personne que tu es aujourd’hui ?

HK : « Je suis né à Roubaix en 1976, fils de parents immigrés d’Algérie. J’ai grandi dans cette ville, la plus pauvre de France, surtout dans ces années 80-90. Mais j’ai eu une jeunesse heureuse. Avec les copains, on a l’impression, avec le recul, d’être passés entre les gouttes. On voyait bien que c’était le désastre autour de nous, mais on vivait joyeusement. J’ai commencé la musique à 14, 15 ans. Le hip-hop débarquait d’outre-Atlantique dans nos quartiers, comme un tsunami.

J’ai choisi de prendre le micro quand d’autres copains se lançaient dans les graffitis, la danse hip-hop, ou le DJing. J’ai commencé dans le rap avec un premier groupe qui s’appelait Juste Cause. À l’époque, on pouvait faire des CD auto-produits qu’on mettait en dépôt-vente… Ça restait dans notre région, mais on était vraiment actifs. Notre premier maxi-CD s’appelait La dette de l’Occident. Notre second, Président, où on mettait un coup de pied dans la fourmilière. » 

➡ Mr Mondialisation : Ta musique était engagée dès le départ ?

HK : « Oui, c’était du rap conscient, mais toujours avec un rapport à la mélodie et au chant. J’ai eu un autre groupe, Peace of Salam, qui est resté dans le milieu amateur. Un combo reggae et hip hop, avec des amis d’enfance. Puis, il y a eu ce projet, MAP, pour Ministère des Affaires populaires. Du rap avec un accordéon, un violon. Tout de suite, ça a explosé. On a eu la reconnaissance du public et même des professionnels.

D’un coup, on est sortis de notre région, on a trouvé un producteur, on a joué dans les plus grands festivals de France. Les gens ont connu MAP avec des morceaux comme Debout la d’dans, Elle est belle la France… Il y a toujours eu ce côté rap conscient, engagé, militant, avec une grande musicalité. » 

➡ Mr Mondialisation : Quand le projet HK est-il né ?

HK : « En 2009. J’ai lancé HK et les Saltimbanks avec l’album Citoyen du monde et des titres comme On lâche rien. J‘avais juste envie de chanter, presque de dire la même chose qu’avec MAP, mais sous une forme un peu différente. HK fonctionne depuis plus de quinze ans de façon assez collégiale. Beaucoup de musiciennes et musiciens sont devenus des amis, des sœurs et des frères de son. Des gens rencontrés sur la route et avec qui le feeling est passé. C’est une grande tribu musicale, une famille. » 

    « Résister, c’est fondamental, mais ce n’est pas suffisant. » 

➡ Mr Mondialisation : Ta musique est une invitation à la fête, à la communion. Est-ce l’une des meilleures façons de résister ?

HK : « Résister, c’est fondamental, mais ce n’est pas suffisant, parce que ça implique d’être sur la défensive. De ne pas se laisser écraser par le rouleau compresseur. Mais pour moi, il faut qu’il y ait autre chose. Il faut un autre ingrédient, une dimension qui est celle de la proposition, de la création, de l’alternative.

En tant qu’artistes, je pense qu’on a notre part à apporter. Surtout dans cette époque où tout est fait pour nous opposer, semer la haine, la discorde. En contrepartie, il faut essayer de bâtir des ponts entre les gens, de maintenir de l’unité partout où c’est possible, des moments et des espaces refuges où les gens peuvent juste être heureux d’être ensemble et de danser ensemble. » 

➡ Mr Mondialisation : D’où ta chanson Danser encore, sortie pendant l’un des confinements dus au Covid… 

HK : « Oui, car on subissait alors une gestion ultra-autoritaire, ultra-sécuritaire. Et là, on se dit : tiens, la démocratie a été kidnappée. Cinq, six personnes dans un bureau décident de ce qui est bien pour des millions, sans aucune forme de discussion. Car l’urgence leur donne la soi-disant légitimité pour le faire. Elle dit tout ça, cette chanson. On est au moment du deuxième confinement, on nous dit que la musique est non-essentielle. Vous pourrez aller au supermarché, vous pourrez faire vos courses, mais la culture n’est pas essentielle.

Ce fut la goutte d’eau, l’absurdité totale. Je crois que le succès de la chanson vient du fait qu’on a été beaucoup à ressentir le même ras-le-bol, le même besoin de dire stop. Comme s’ils avaient décidé qu’au XXIe siècle, manger, boire et dormir suffisaient à faire de nous des êtres humains. Or ce n’est pas ce qu’on est en tant qu’individu, et en tant que société. On a donc balancé cette chanson comme ça, filmée avec le téléphone… On n’aurait jamais pensé que ça allait résonner à ce point. » 

➡ Mr Mondialisation : D’autant qu’elle résonne toujours, des années après.

HK : « Oui, mais je me suis contenté de faire ce que j’ai toujours fait. Quand quelque chose me touche, me révolte, m’indigne, ou au contraire suscite des émotions positives, j’écris une chanson pour faire passer cette émotion. Et quand je chante « Ne soyons pas impressionnables / Par tous ces gens déraisonnables / Vendeurs de peur en abondance / Angoissants, jusqu’à l’indécence… », ça marche, ça crée une résonance auprès des gens. » 

➡ Mr Mondialisation : Plus récemment, tu as pris le micro à Saint-Denis pour défendre son nouveau maire, Bally Bagayoko. Est-ce que c’était une évidence pour toi ?

HK : « C’était une évidence, oui. Il n’y a rien de pire pour moi que d’être spectateur. Là, je voulais m’exprimer, peu importe l’utilité ou l’impact. Il s’avère que j’étais à Paris le même jour, pour une autre manifestation. D’habitude, on me sollicite. Là, c’est moi qui ai appelé les copains pour proposer de venir chanter, affirmer ma solidarité, et qu’on soit le plus nombreux possible. Bally est devenu un symbole.

J’étais très heureux de pouvoir lui dire en direct : Tu es notre fierté. À nous, enfants des quartiers populaires, et pas juste enfants de l’immigration. Cette fierté, elle est également due à la dignité, la classe avec laquelle il a répondu à tout cet acharnement. »

➡ Mr Mondialisation : Tu as senti un vrai élan populaire ? Et un peu d’espoir ?

HK : « Clairement. Les médias ont été obligés d’en parler, mais je pense qu’ils ont vraiment minimisé. De l’intérieur, c’était incroyable, et ça donne beaucoup espoir. On parlait de résistance… Quand tu vois ce marteau-piqueur qu’est l’empire Bolloré, ce bashing de toutes nos idées, nos valeurs, nos combats depuis toutes ces années… Ils essaient de faire croire à la population que nous, ceux qui résistent, on ne compte pas. » 
 
➡ Mr Mondialisation : La main-mise de quelques-uns sur les médias, c’est un fait que tu constates personnellement ? 

HK : « Depuis dix ans, je constate ce processus d’invisibilisation. C’est criant. Au début, j’ai juste vu qu’on commençait à disparaître petit à petit des médias alors que beaucoup de gens nous suivaient, qu’on avait de l’actualité… Concrètement, on ne nous a jamais dit « Non, on ne veut pas de vous. » Mais il y avait toujours une bonne raison pour ne plus nous inviter. Ça, on l’a constaté et pendant un moment, on ne le comprenait pas.

    « Aujourd’hui, on comprend les mécanismes de monopole des médias par une certaine caste. » 

Aujourd’hui, on comprend les mécanismes de monopole des médias par une certaine caste et en plus, au service d’une idéologie raciste, suprémaciste, xénophobe. Nous, on incarne exactement l’antithèse donc pourquoi nous laisser la parole, nous offrir la possibilité de répondre ?

Malheureusement, ces gens-là ont un impact, puisqu’ils sont matin, midi et soir à la télé, à la radio. Cette propagande, à force, elle fait des dégâts. Alors, rassembler des dizaines de milliers de personnes lors de rassemblements spontanés, ça nous rappelle qu’on est nombreux. Que ce soit pour Bally ou pour la journée du 10 septembre 2025… On est plus nombreux que ce qu’on veut nous faire croire. » 

➡ Mr Mondialisation : Mais la difficulté reste de réussir à s’organiser. Et ça, ils le savent très bien… 

HK : « Oui, c’est à nous de trouver des solutions. C’est la part qui nous incombe, de se dire : Comment peut-on faire ? Il n’y a qu’un seul chemin, de toute façon, c’est sûr. » 

➡ Mr Mondialisation : Tu as vu plusieurs générations grandir en France. Quels espoirs as-tu pour celles qui arrivent ?

HK : « Je vois ma fille aînée, qui a 27 ans et est ultra militante, active, radicale. Plus que moi sans doute ! Je les vois eux, et puis moi, en train de devenir un vieux dépassé (rires) ! Mais je le vois avec joie. Ils sont là. On va tous mettre la main à la pâte, et ça me donne beaucoup d’espoir. Le contexte général est complexe : la main-mise sur les médias, ce rouleau compresseur, et nous, avec nos petits moyens. Tant qu’il y a de la lutte, il y a de l’espoir. Tant qu’il y a de la vie, il y a du combat. » 

➡ Mr Mondialisation : Tu joues aussi bien dans des salles moyennes que dans les quartiers, sur la place publique. Ressens-tu toujours le même élan ? 

HK : « Oui parce que, quel soit l’endroit, on arrive avec ce qu’on est, notre sincérité, donc ça connecte toujours. Elle résonne au fin fond de nos campagnes, quand on fait les bals paysans, comme au cœur des quartiers. Ma musique, ce n’est pas spontanément ce que les jeunes des quartiers vont écouter. Mais à chaque fois qu’on y joue, il se passe des moments extraordinaires. Il y a les daronnes, les darons, les enfants, et puis les ados qui se retrouvent embarqués par l’ambiance. Il y a même les chibanis, les anciennes, les anciens. Tu sens qu’il y a quelque chose qui prend. » 

    « il y a encore une immense majorité de gens dans notre pays qui veulent juste vivre ensemble de façon heureuse, apaisée, respectueuse. » 

➡ Mr Mondialisation : Des projets en ce sens à venir ? 

HK : « On va jouer chez nous dans le Nord pour les 40 ans de l’association de la Goutte d’or. J’adore jouer sur la place publique. Dans des endroits différents, pour des gens différents, en disant les mêmes choses. Parce que finalement, on aspire aux mêmes choses. Malgré la propagande puissante, il y a encore une immense majorité de gens dans notre pays qui veulent juste vivre ensemble de façon heureuse, apaisée, respectueuse. Notre travail, c’est de contrer ça, nourrir le vivre ensemble et le mettre en visibilité le plus possible. » 
Mr Mondialisation : Un dernier mot pour les lecteurs et lectrices de Mr Mondialisation ?

HK : « On continue, on lâche rien ! Aujourd’hui, comme hier, et comme demain. »

Travel memory: Good morning, dear virtual adventurers! Today is Saturday, 23 May 2026, and I look forward to welcoming you on yet another unforgettable journey. Our virtual destination today is Germany, where we will be exploring the enchanting Niederburg Kobern. We will discover its history, admire its architecture and delve into the legends that have swirled within its walls for centuries. So, without further ado: Let’s go!

Echoes of Time: The Mystique and Splendour of Niederburg Kobern - Perched high above the breathtaking Moselle Valley, Niederburg Kobern stands as an impressive testament to medieval ingenuity, power and tradition. Once a steadfast fortress protecting trade routes and borders, this hidden gem in Rhineland-Palatinate now invites us to relive the stories of knights, noble families and ecclesiastical intrigues through its weathered ruins.

A landscape steeped in history - Nestled on a rocky ridge some 150 metres above the charming village of Kobern, Kobern Lower Castle offers a breathtaking panoramic view of the Moselle Valley. The castle shares this elevated site with the Oberburg Kobern, which lies 50 metres higher, and the Matthias Chapel – an architectural treasure of medieval construction. Together, they form a site of great historical and strategic importance. The arrangement of the Lower and Upper Castles suggests a deliberate defensive hierarchy. Their commanding positions served not only to protect but also to control the trade routes vital to the medieval economy.

An architectural legacy - The Lower Castle itself bears witness to the brilliance of medieval engineering. Its almond-shaped structure tells a story of enduring resilience, with features designed to withstand both natural decay and military assault. The centrepiece of this fortress is its three-storey keep, which rises 20 metres into the sky and exudes strength with its thick stone walls. Strategically, the entrance to the tower was positioned 10 metres above the ground to make access difficult for attackers – a testament to the sophisticated defensive measures of the time. Once inside, visitors found a safe haven within its sturdy walls. Surrounding the keep were living quarters, a cistern that ensured the inhabitants’ survival during sieges, and outer defensive walls with a protective forecourt. Although much of the castle now lies in ruins, restoration work has brought parts of its former splendour back to life, including sections of the great hall and the battlements.

A Chronicle of Power and Decline - The history of Niederburg Kobern reflects the rise and fall of noble families closely intertwined with ecclesiastical powers. Originally built in the mid-12th century, it became a symbol of feudal loyalty when its owner swore allegiance to the Archbishop of Trier. Over time, the castle passed through various noble families, most notably the Isenburg-Kobern family, whose dynasty came to an end in the 13th century. Following the death of Cecilia, the heiress of Isenburg-Kobern, the estate passed to Friedrich II of Neuerburg of the Viander family. However, like its predecessors, this family eventually died out, resulting in the castle falling under the control of the Archbishopric of Trier. In the late 17th century, French troops ravaged the fortress during the Nine Years’ War, destroying its defences and leaving behind the ruins we see today.

Legends Haunting the Stones - Given this rich history, it is no wonder that Niederburg Kobern has inspired myths and ghost stories over the years. Locals tell of ghostly knights who guard the castle on moonlit nights, bound to the land by duty and memory. Hidden treasures, buried in the chaos of war, lure adventurers and explorers alike to scour the depths of the ruins. One legend tells of Cecilia, the last of the Isenburg-Kobern family, who wanders the ridge between Niederburg and Oberburg. It is said that her spirit roams in search of lost justice, or perhaps simply to mourn the legacy her family left behind – a sombre yet fascinating tale that adds to the mystique of the place.

A visit for visitors - Today, Niederburg Kobern invites visitors to experience its timeless charm. Unlike many other medieval ruins, admission to this castle remains free, offering adventurers the rare opportunity to explore it at their leisure. The narrow path leading up from the Mühlbach Valley offers a picturesque walk through dense foliage and culminates in breathtaking views of the Moselle, rewarding every step of the ascent. Once at the ruins, visitors can climb the tower, view the remains of the great hall and reflect on the architectural masterpieces that once characterised this fortress. The castle’s designation as a protected cultural monument underscores its significance as part of the region’s cultural heritage.

Timeless Paths and Echoes of the Past - Amidst the ruins of Niederburg Kobern, visitors feel the weight of history and the whisper of forgotten tales. It is more than just stone and mortar – it is a gateway to a time when knights strode through the corridors and noble families shaped the fate of the regions. Their legacy, preserved through restoration and storytelling, continues to inspire all those seeking a connection to the past. Whether you are drawn by the beauty of the Moselle Valley, fascinated by medieval history, or captivated by tales of knights and nobles – Niederburg Kobern promises an unforgettable journey.

Sentiers intemporels et échos du passé – Au milieu des ruines de Niederburg Kobern, les visiteurs ressentent le poids de l’histoire et le murmure de contes oubliés. 29 January 2026

PAS menyanggah kenyataan Muhyiddin Yassin tentang persetujuan parti itu untuk memansuhkan jawatan Pengerusi PN dan menggantikannya dengan penubuhan dua badan lain iaitu Majlis Presiden dan Majlis Eksekutif.

Presiden PAS, Haji Hadi Awang berkata, isu itu sama sekali tidak pernah dibincangkan dan dipersetujui oleh PAS termasuk dalam pertemuan dengan Muhyiddin pada 16 Januari lalu.

Jelas beliau, PAS kekal dengan pendirian bahawa jawatan Pengerusi PN hendaklah dikekalkan dan tidak dimansuhkan serta diurus tadbir seperti mana yang diperuntukkan dalam Fasal 8.3(l) Perlembagaan PN.

Berhubung cadangan untuk pindaan Perlembagaan berkaitan penstrukturan PN khususnya mengenai Majlis Presiden, PAS tegas Haji Hadi,  mengulangi saranan bahawa Majlis Presiden hendaklah bertindak sebagai ‘Badan Penasihat’ dan ‘Pengawal Selia’ dalam memelihara dasar-dasar dan hala tuju PN.

“Adapun mengenai kenyataan Muhyiddin bahawa “Dengan penstrukturan semula PN, jawatan Pengerusi Perikatan Nasional dimansuhkan dan hal pelantikan Pengerusi PN tidak lagi berbangkit”, saya ingin menegaskan bahawa isu ini sama sekali tidak pernah dibincangkan dan dipersetujui oleh pihak kami termasuk dalam pertemuan pada 16 Januari 2026,” katanya dalam satu kenyataan.

Haji Hadi menambah, sebagai rujukan asas berkaitan Majlis Eksekutif PN, Pas menggariskan cadangan yang mana Majlis Tertinggi PN (MTPN) harus menjadi Majlis Eksekutir (ME) yang bertanggungjawab melaksanakan segala perancangan parti.

Ia, ujar beliau, termasuk dari sudut perorganisasian, pentadbiran dan strategi bagi memperkukuhkan parti gabungan itu terutama dalam menghadapi pilihan raya negeri (PRN) mahu pun pilihan raya umum (PRU).

Selain itu, kata Haji Hadi, kuasa dan fungsi ME hendaklah digariskan dengan terperinci yang turut diselaraskan dengan idealisma dan perancangan Parti-Parti Anggota.

“Dalam menjalankan fungsinya, ME mempunyai akauntabiliti kepada Majlis Presiden yang berperanan memantau dan mengawal selia ME dari segi dasar dan hala tuju yang ditetapkan oleh parti.

“Berdasarkan kepada perkara di atas, maka adalah menjadi pandangan dan pendirian PAS bahawa Majlis Presiden hendaklah bertindak sebagai ‘Badan Penasihat’ dan ‘Pengawal Selia’ dalam memelihara dasar-dasar dan hala tuju PN.

“(Selain itu) Majlis Tertinggi PN hendaklah juga menjadi Majlis Eksekutif PN yang bertindak sebagai ‘Badan Pelaksana’ dalam segala urusan pentadbiran dan strategi parti, selaras dengan Fasal 8 Perlembagaan PN,” katanya lagi dalam kenyataan dua halaman itu.

Berdasarkan huraian Haji Hadi di atas, adalah jelas ia berlawanan dengan kenyataan Muhyiddin semalam.

Mengimbas konflik dalam PN sejak Muhyiddin mengumumkan perletakan jawatannya bertarikh 1 Januari lalu, kekalutan yang timbul dan berlarutan hingga kini adalah kerana Presiden Bersatu itu tidak benar-benar ikhlas mahu berundur dan seolah-olah sedang mencari laluan u-turn untuk kembali menerajui PN.

Sepatutnya, setelah meletakkan jawatan, Muhyiddin mestilah benar-bemar ingin beundur dan melepaskan dirinya daripada PN.

Tidak bolehkah dikekalkan PN seperti sedia ada dan sebagaimana Muhyiddin mengetuainya sebelum ini?

Travel memory: Good morning, friends of European history. Today is Friday, 22 May 2026. I invite you on a virtual journey to Georgia to explore Skhvilo Fortress, a medieval gem that has fallen into obscurity over the centuries. I hope you enjoy today’s exploration – let’s begin!

In the heart of Georgia, amidst the breathtaking landscape of the Shida Kartli region, stands Skhvilo Fortress – a remarkable relic of medieval architecture and a silent witness to past events. Built in the 14th century, this fortress originally served as the noble residence of the Amilakhvari family before being used primarily for defensive purposes. Although its significance has waned over time, Skhvilo Fortress remains a fascinating structure steeped in historical narratives, architectural mastery and tales of resilience.

An architectural marvel - Skhvilo Fortress attracts attention not only through its imposing presence but also through its ingenious construction. Perched on a mountain ridge, it is flanked to the west by the gorge of the River Rekhula and to the east by the Tiriponi Valley. This natural fortification made it considerably more difficult for potential attackers to breach the defences, making the fortress an impressive defensive stronghold. The structure itself is approximately 45 metres long and 20 metres wide, with a height of up to 14 metres across three to four storeys. The outer walls – whose thickness varies between two and four metres – are crowned with battlements designed to protect medieval archers. An additional wooden walkway, supported by corbels, further enhanced the defences. Loopholes at strategic points allowed the defenders to strike with precision whilst remaining protected themselves. Distinctive bastions enhanced the fortress’s resilience. Two semicircular bastions reinforced the western end, whilst the eastern side featured four bastions projecting from the main wall. Access to the fortress was severely restricted; the sole entrance on the south-western side required a makeshift wooden ladder, ideal for keeping intruders at bay. Within the complex, features such as a small inner courtyard provided additional security by blocking direct access to the surrounding buildings. Two towers – the five-storey watchtower to the north and a smaller southern tower – served as vantage points for observing approaching enemies. The living quarters adjoined the defensive walls and were complemented by a compact two-storey church and a water reservoir, ingeniously fed via an aqueduct. Furthermore, traces of siege tunnels and underground passages point to the fortress’s turbulent past, in which battles shook its foundations and tested the endurance of its inhabitants.

From noble residence to battlefield: a history steeped in the past - Skhvilo Fortress is closely linked to the Amilakhvari family, whose lineage played a central role in Georgian feudal history. The estate became their fiefdom in the 14th century and symbolised both their status and their strategic acumen. Originally a noble residence, Skhvilo retained its importance until the 16th century, when the family moved to Kvemo Chala and relocated their seat of power to the newly built Amilakhvari Castle. Following this move, the fortress served exclusively as a military stronghold and was the scene of historical upheavals and power struggles. Among the notable episodes is a 17th-century clash in which Iota Amilakhvari famously repelled King Rostom of Kartli. In later years, under the leadership of Givi Amilakhvari, the fortress played a decisive role in the resistance against Persian troops. However, the gradual decline of the Amilakhvari dynasty in the 18th century led to the fortress being abandoned.

Legends that enchant the walls of Skhvilo - Beyond its historical significance, Skhvilo Fortress is steeped in captivating legends that have been passed down through the generations. Some tales speak of vast treasures hidden within its underground labyrinths, attracting adventurers eager to uncover its secrets. Others recount the heroic defences and triumphs of the Amilakhvari family against invaders, portraying them as valiant protectors of Georgian sovereignty. A moving legend surrounds the small church within the fortress, which is said to house a sacred artefact that granted divine protection to its inhabitants. Although evidence for these claims is scarce, they lend the fortress a mystical allure that continues to capture the imagination.

Skhvilo Today: Preservation and Cultural Value - Although centuries have passed since its glory days, Skhvilo Fortress has remained relatively intact – a testament to the craftsmanship and ingenuity of Georgian architects. Its architectural splendour and historical heritage make it an important destination for visitors seeking a connection to the past whilst admiring the breathtaking landscape that surrounds it.

Skhvilo Fortress is far more than a medieval ruin – it is a gateway to a bygone era, rich in political intrigue, architectural brilliance and human perseverance. No coração da Geórgia, no meio da paisagem deslumbrante da região de Shida Kartli, ergue-se a Fortaleza de Skhvilo – uma relíquia notável da arquitetura medieval e uma testemunha silenciosa de acontecimentos passados. Construída no século XIV, esta fortaleza serviu originalmente como residência nobre da família Amilakhvari, antes de ser utilizada principalmente para fins defensivos. Embora a sua importância tenha diminuído com o tempo, a Fortaleza de Skhvilo continua a ser uma estrutura fascinante, rica em narrativas históricas, mestria arquitetónica e histórias de resiliência.

Uma maravilha arquitetónica – a Fortaleza de Skhvilo atrai a atenção não só pela sua presença imponente, mas também pela sua construção engenhosa. Situada no cume de uma montanha, é ladeada a oeste pelo desfiladeiro do rio Rekhula e a leste pelo Vale de Tiriponi. Esta fortificação natural tornou consideravelmente mais difícil para potenciais atacantes violarem as defesas, tornando a fortaleza uma impressionante fortaleza defensiva. A estrutura em si tem aproximadamente 45 metros de comprimento e 20 metros de largura, com uma altura de até 14 metros distribuída por três a quatro andares. As paredes exteriores — cuja espessura varia entre dois e quatro metros — são coroadas por ameias concebidas para proteger os arqueiros medievais. Uma passarela de madeira adicional, suportada por mísulas, reforçava ainda mais as defesas. As seteiras em pontos estratégicos permitiam aos defensores atacar com precisão, mantendo-se eles próprios protegidos. Bastiões distintivos aumentavam a resiliência da fortaleza. Dois bastiões semicirculares reforçavam a extremidade ocidental, enquanto o lado oriental apresentava quatro bastiões que se projetavam da parede principal. O acesso à fortaleza era severamente restrito; a única entrada no lado sudoeste exigia uma escada de madeira improvisada, ideal para manter os intrusos à distância. Dentro do complexo, elementos como um pequeno pátio interior proporcionavam segurança adicional, bloqueando o acesso direto aos edifícios circundantes. Duas torres — a torre de vigia de cinco andares a norte e uma torre sul mais pequena — serviam como pontos estratégicos para observar os inimigos que se aproximavam. Os aposentos adjacentes às muralhas defensivas eram complementados por uma igreja compacta de dois andares e um reservatório de água, engenhosamente alimentado por um aqueduto. Além disso, vestígios de túneis de cerco e passagens subterrâneas apontam para o passado turbulento da fortaleza, em que as batalhas abalaram as suas fundações e puseram à prova a resistência dos seus habitantes.

De residência nobre a campo de batalha: uma história rica no passado – a Fortaleza de Skhvilo está intimamente ligada à família Amilakhvari, cuja linhagem desempenhou um papel central na história feudal georgiana. A propriedade tornou-se o seu feudo no século XIV e simbolizava tanto o seu estatuto como a sua perspicácia estratégica. Originalmente uma residência nobre, Skhvilo manteve a sua importância até ao século XVI, quando a família se mudou para Kvemo Chala e transferiu a sua sede de poder para o recém-construído Castelo de Amilakhvari. Na sequência desta mudança, a fortaleza serviu exclusivamente como reduto militar e foi palco de convulsões históricas e lutas pelo poder. Entre os episódios notáveis destaca-se um confronto do século XVII em que Iota Amilakhvari repeliu de forma célebre o rei Rostom de Kartli. Nos anos seguintes, sob a liderança de Givi Amilakhvari, a fortaleza desempenhou um papel decisivo na resistência contra as tropas persas. No entanto, o declínio gradual da dinastia Amilakhvari no século XVIII levou ao abandono da fortaleza.

Lendas que encantam as muralhas de Skhvilo - Para além do seu significado histórico, a Fortaleza de Skhvilo está repleta de lendas cativantes que têm sido transmitidas de geração em geração. Algumas histórias falam de vastos tesouros escondidos nos seus labirintos subterrâneos, atraindo aventureiros ansiosos por desvendar os seus segredos. Outras relatam as heroicas defesas e triunfos da família Amilakhvari contra os invasores, retratando-os como valentes protetores da soberania georgiana. Uma lenda comovente envolve a pequena igreja dentro da fortaleza, que, segundo se diz, alberga um artefacto sagrado que concedia proteção divina aos seus habitantes. Embora as provas para estas alegações sejam escassas, conferem à fortaleza um encanto místico que continua a cativar a imaginação.

Skhvilo Hoje: Preservação e Valor Cultural - Embora tenham passado séculos desde os seus dias de glória, a Fortaleza de Skhvilo permaneceu relativamente intacta – um testemunho da habilidade e engenhosidade dos arquitetos georgianos. No entanto, tal como muitos locais históricos, também ela é vulnerável à devastação do tempo e à decadência, sublinhando a necessidade urgente de trabalhos de restauro para salvaguardar este tesouro cultural. Skhvilo é mais do que apenas um edifício: encarna a história turbulenta da Geórgia e reflete a resiliência do seu povo. O seu esplendor arquitetónico e património histórico tornam-na um destino importante para visitantes que procuram uma ligação ao passado, enquanto admiram a paisagem deslumbrante que a rodeia.

A Fortaleza de Skhvilo é muito mais do que uma ruína medieval – é uma porta de entrada para uma era passada, rica em intrigas políticas, brilhantismo arquitetónico e perseverança humana. Seja como aventureiros, historiadores ou viajantes curiosos – é nossa responsabilidade valorizar e preservar tais locais. Estas pedras, estas paredes, são contadoras de histórias de uma era passada, e as suas mensagens ecoam através dos séculos, lembrando-nos de não esquecer.

Travel memory: Good morning, virtual time travellers! Today is Sunday, 24 May 2026. My name is Freddy Kalder and I’m absolutely delighted to take you on a journey to the enchanting ruins of Tourbillon Castle in Switzerland. Perched high above the old town of Sion, this majestic site sparks the imagination with its tales of history, resilience and legends. Grab a cup of coffee, make yourself comfortable and let’s embark on this adventure together!

The majestic ruins of Tourbillon: A journey through history and legend - Perched high above the Swiss canton of Valais, Tourbillon Castle sits atop a striking hill, commanding the view. Its counterpart, the Basilica of Valeria, rises on a neighbouring peak, creating an unforgettable vista over the landscape of Sion. Whilst the basilica exudes religious elegance, Tourbillon radiates power, mystery and fascination. Today, the castle stands as a testament to centuries of human ingenuity, resilience and myth, inviting us to explore its ruins and unravel the secrets engraved in its stones.

A hill with ancient roots - Long before Tourbillon Castle was built, the hill on which it stands was a place of significance. Finds discovered by archaeologists suggest that people inhabited this site as early as the 5th millennium BC. In the Middle Ages, the hill’s strategic value came to the fore, as it served as a vantage point for defence during conflicts. The remains of its ancient keep – a fortified tower – bear witness to these early efforts to protect the region. Records show that guards were stationed here as early as 1270 to guard against potential attacks. The hill’s role as a defensive structure laid the foundation for what would later become a seat of geopolitical power: Tourbillon Castle.

From Fortress to Centre of Power - Construction of Tourbillon Castle began in the late 13th century under Bishop Boniface Challant. However, building such an imposing structure took time; historical records suggest that much of the castle was not completed until around 1307. Its construction coincided with turbulent political unrest between the bishopric and the nobility, particularly under Peter IV of Turn. The castle, built to protect the town of Sion, symbolised both physical security and the bishop’s authority in the region. In the Middle Ages, its massive stone walls served not only as protection but also as a demonstration of power – a dual role that was central to medieval politics.

Splendour and danger in the Middle Ages - Tourbillon Castle quickly became an important residence for the bishops, particularly during the summer months when it offered refuge from danger. Yet its halls were not spared from conflict. During the War of Raron in 1417, angry Upper Valaisans looted and severely damaged the fortress. A restoration led by Bishop William III of Raron brought the castle back to life in the mid-15th century, including the redesign of its chapel – a sign of the intertwining of faith and power in that era. Yet the splendour of Tourbillon was often under threat. Throughout the Middle Ages, it was subjected to occupations, attacks and ultimately destruction, forcing those who lived within its protective walls to adapt time and again.

The tragic fire of 1788: A turning point - On 24 May 1788, tragedy struck. A violent storm swept through the Rhône Valley, sparking a fire that ravaged Sion and its landmarks. Among the casualties were Tourbillon Castle and Majoria Castle, the bishop’s residences. The inferno lasted only three hours, yet caused irreparable damage, leaving ruins where splendour once stood. Attempts to rebuild the castle failed amidst major upheavals, particularly the French Revolution, which transformed the region’s political and economic landscape. From that point on, Tourbillon Castle became a relic – a witness to a bygone era.

Tourbillon today: A preserved memory - Despite its destruction, Tourbillon Castle retains its cultural significance. It was declared a monument of national importance in 1907 and is carefully preserved by the Fondation du Château de Tourbillon. Since 1977, the ruins have been protected under the Hague Conventions and now serve as a place of discovery, remembrance and reflection. From March to November, visitors can explore the castle ruins whilst enjoying the panoramic view of the Rhone Valley below.

Myths and Legends of Tourbillon - The haunting beauty of Tourbillon has inspired countless legends and further enhanced its allure. Locals whisper of ghostly bishops who wander through the ruins under the full moon, seeking peace in the shadows. Another tale speaks of a treasure buried deep beneath the stones – hidden riches that have eluded discovery for generations. Such myths lend the fortress an air of mystique, transforming Tourbillon from a purely historical site into something magical – a crossroads between fact and folklore that attracts adventurers and dreamers alike.

A Monument to Resilience - At its core, Tourbillon Castle symbolises the transience of human power and the enduring constancy of nature. Wars, storms and revolutions have ravaged its walls, yet its spirit endures, reminding all visitors that history is never truly forgotten. Anyone climbing the castle’s steps today embarks on a journey through centuries of ambition, survival and loss. From the breathtaking views of the Rhône Valley to the eerie silence in the crumbling halls – every moment at Tourbillon is a reminder of humanity’s resilience and its connection to the past.

Our virtual journey to Tourbillon Castle reveals not just a historical ruin, but a living symbol of change and permanence. Within its stones, we find stories that endure through time – tales of struggle, hope and renewal. Whether you come for the history, the landscape or the legends: Tourbillon Castle is a destination that leaves a lasting impression.

I hope you enjoyed today’s adventure! Join me tomorrow for another exciting exploration. Until then, I wish you a wonderful day. Your companion on journeys through time, Freddy Kalder

Sa contrepartie, la basilique de Valeria, s’élève sur un sommet voisin, offrant une vue inoubliable sur le paysage de Sion. De tels mythes confèrent à la forteresse une aura de mystère, transformant Tourbillon d’un site purement historique en un lieu magique – un carrefour entre réalité et folklore qui attire aussi bien les aventuriers que les rêveurs.

Un monument à la résilience - Au fond, le château de Tourbillon symbolise le caractère éphémère du pouvoir humain et la constance durable de la nature. Des vues à couper le souffle sur la vallée du Rhône au silence inquiétant des salles en ruines – chaque instant passé à Tourbillon est un rappel de la résilience de l’humanité et de son lien avec le passé.

Notre voyage virtuel au château de Tourbillon ne révèle pas seulement une ruine historique, mais un symbole vivant de changement et de permanence. Travel memory: Good morning, friends of European history. Today is Friday, 22 May 2026. I invite you on a virtual journey to Georgia to explore Skhvilo Fortress, a medieval gem that has fallen into obscurity over the centuries. I hope you enjoy today’s exploration – let’s begin!

In the heart of Georgia, amidst the breathtaking landscape of the Shida Kartli region, stands Skhvilo Fortress – a remarkable relic of medieval architecture and a silent witness to past events. Built in the 14th century, this fortress originally served as the noble residence of the Amilakhvari family before being used primarily for defensive purposes. Although its significance has waned over time, Skhvilo Fortress remains a fascinating structure steeped in historical narratives, architectural mastery and tales of resilience.

An architectural marvel - Skhvilo Fortress attracts attention not only through its imposing presence but also through its ingenious construction. Perched on a mountain ridge, it is flanked to the west by the gorge of the River Rekhula and to the east by the Tiriponi Valley. This natural fortification made it considerably more difficult for potential attackers to breach the defences, making the fortress an impressive defensive stronghold. The structure itself is approximately 45 metres long and 20 metres wide, with a height of up to 14 metres across three to four storeys. The outer walls – whose thickness varies between two and four metres – are crowned with battlements designed to protect medieval archers. An additional wooden walkway, supported by corbels, further enhanced the defences. Loopholes at strategic points allowed the defenders to strike with precision whilst remaining protected themselves. Distinctive bastions enhanced the fortress’s resilience. Two semicircular bastions reinforced the western end, whilst the eastern side featured four bastions projecting from the main wall. Access to the fortress was severely restricted; the sole entrance on the south-western side required a makeshift wooden ladder, ideal for keeping intruders at bay. Within the complex, features such as a small inner courtyard provided additional security by blocking direct access to the surrounding buildings. Two towers – the five-storey watchtower to the north and a smaller southern tower – served as vantage points for observing approaching enemies. The living quarters adjoined the defensive walls and were complemented by a compact two-storey church and a water reservoir, ingeniously fed via an aqueduct. Furthermore, traces of siege tunnels and underground passages point to the fortress’s turbulent past, in which battles shook its foundations and tested the endurance of its inhabitants.

From noble residence to battlefield: a history steeped in the past - Skhvilo Fortress is closely linked to the Amilakhvari family, whose lineage played a central role in Georgian feudal history. The estate became their fiefdom in the 14th century and symbolised both their status and their strategic acumen. Originally a noble residence, Skhvilo retained its importance until the 16th century, when the family moved to Kvemo Chala and relocated their seat of power to the newly built Amilakhvari Castle. Following this move, the fortress served exclusively as a military stronghold and was the scene of historical upheavals and power struggles. Among the notable episodes is a 17th-century clash in which Iota Amilakhvari famously repelled King Rostom of Kartli. In later years, under the leadership of Givi Amilakhvari, the fortress played a decisive role in the resistance against Persian troops. However, the gradual decline of the Amilakhvari dynasty in the 18th century led to the fortress being abandoned.

Legends that enchant the walls of Skhvilo - Beyond its historical significance, Skhvilo Fortress is steeped in captivating legends that have been passed down through the generations. Some tales speak of vast treasures hidden within its underground labyrinths, attracting adventurers eager to uncover its secrets. Others recount the heroic defences and triumphs of the Amilakhvari family against invaders, portraying them as valiant protectors of Georgian sovereignty. A moving legend surrounds the small church within the fortress, which is said to house a sacred artefact that granted divine protection to its inhabitants. Although evidence for these claims is scarce, they lend the fortress a mystical allure that continues to capture the imagination.

Skhvilo Today: Preservation and Cultural Value - Although centuries have passed since its glory days, Skhvilo Fortress has remained relatively intact – a testament to the craftsmanship and ingenuity of Georgian architects. Yet, like many historic sites, it too is vulnerable to the ravages of time and decay, underscoring the urgent need for restoration work to safeguard this cultural treasure. Skhvilo is more than just a building: it embodies Georgia’s turbulent history and reflects the resilience of its people. Its architectural splendour and historical heritage make it an important destination for visitors seeking a connection to the past whilst admiring the breathtaking landscape that surrounds it.

Skhvilo Fortress is far more than a medieval ruin – it is a gateway to a bygone era, rich in political intrigue, architectural brilliance and human perseverance. Whether as adventurers, historians or curious travellers – it is our responsibility to cherish and preserve such sites. These stones, these walls, are storytellers of a bygone age, and their messages echo through the centuries, reminding us not to forget.

Thank you very much for joining me on today’s virtual expedition. I hope you found it just as exciting as I did. See you tomorrow – stay curious and have a wonderful day. Yours, Freddy Kalder
